Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran a quick internal heartbeat with product and ops and they're comfortable moving off Compact to a Throughput-oriented plan for the next 12 months — the classifier latency improvements are worth the uplift. Before we lock anything in we have two questions:

1) Feature bundling: we currently rely on the "structured-output" and "function-calls" features. Can those be bundled into the mid-tier (Throughput+) without an add-on? If not, what is the incremental unit cost?

2) Rollback/stepdown: we want a clean rollback path if usage doesn't materialize in Q3. What are the downgrade proration mechanics and how do feature entitlements behave after a downgrade?

I'm attaching a draft mutual action plan (WB-MAP-v2.pdf) and a short usage extract (usage-report-q2.csv) for context.

Appreciate a short summary we can take to procurement — looking for price bands + one recommended conservative path.

Subject: Re: Plan swap - moving from Compact -> Throughput + bundling ask

Alicia — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Short answers up front: yes, we can include structured-output and function-calls in a Throughput+ bundle; and we can offer a 60-day rollback window with pro-rate credits for committed throughput if you exercise a downgrade within that period. Details below.

Summary (for procurement):
- Recommended path: Throughput+ 12-month term, with a pilot ramp for Q3 (start at 50% committed throughput, true-up at month 3).
- Discount bands: 15% off list at 12-month commit (standard), 20% off with a 30% ARR uplift commitment + early payment. We can do one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of committed spend for pilots.
- Feature bundling: structured-output and function-calls included in Throughput+ at no extra per-feature fee (they count toward request/VCU usage but not charged as separate line items).
- Rollback: within 60 days we allow stepdown to Compact with pro-rated credit on the remaining committed throughput (we calculate credit by remaining tokens of committed throughput; any feature entitlements tied to Throughput+ remain for 30 days after downgrade to allow migration). After 30 days post-downgrade entitlements revert unless rolled into an add-on.

I'm looping in Ben to confirm technical entitlements and Kimberly for legal/proration language. Would a short vendor summary doc + price band in a single page be enough for your procurement kick-off? I can turn this into a 1-pager and attach the amended MAP.

Thanks,
Hiro
Hiro Tanaka

Redwood Inference

Alicia / team — quick technical clarification from engineering ops:

- Structured-output and function-calls are feature flags that gate runtime behavior. For Throughput+, we will enable them at the tenant level for the term of the commitment. They will not add an extra charge beyond token usage.
- If you downgrade: the flags remain enabled for 30 days, during which KV cache warms and any pipeline rewrites can be completed. After 30 days the flags will be disabled automatically unless an add-on is purchased.
- Performance guardrail: to protect your latency SLO during peak bursts we recommend keeping prefix KV caching enabled and restricting large-batch jobs during the 60-day pilot ramp. Our recommended default batch size for your workload is 8 tokens/req.

I'll also attach a short example of entitlement language we use in contracts (I'll drop that into the MAP Hiro produces).

Ben
